key_claim: A heat pump moves heat instead of making it, so it can deliver more heat energy than the electricity it uses.

slides.headline: Your heat pump is a fridge running backwards.
It moves heat, it doesn't make it
slides.body: A heat pump pulls warmth from outside air, even cold air, and pumps it indoors.

slides.headline: Up to three times the heat
slides.body: Moving heat takes less energy than making it, so you can get about three units of heat for each unit of power.

figure.title: A heat pump gives about 3x the heat

slides.headline: Flip a valve, get cooling
slides.body: In summer a reversing valve swaps the flow, and the same machine cools your home.
